content.text: The text reviews gastric dilatation, intestinal indigestion, constipation, enteralgia, and acute/chronic intestinal catarrh. Gastric dilatation may result from stenosis or muscular atony, causing delayed vomiting, fermentation, retained food, and malnutrition; diagnosis is clinical and treatment emphasizes diet and stomach-tube lavage. Intestinal indigestion reflects impaired bile, pancreatic, or intestinal digestion, producing gas, pain, altered stools, constipation/diarrhea, anemia, and nervous symptoms. Constipation arises from diet, inactivity, disease, obstruction, or laxative abuse; management prioritizes regular habits, exercise, hydration, diet, and cautious enemas or laxatives. Enteralgia causes neuralgic umbilical pain, while catarrh produces inflammation and diarrhea. Rest, restricted diets, hygiene, climate change, travel to seashores or mountains, and stays at mineral or hot springs are repeatedly recommended.
